sources.title: System Design Primer: Asynchronism, message queues, task queues and back pressure
sources.supportRationale: Required core conceptual/interview-study reference, inspected 2026-11-17; historical product comparisons are not adopted as current guarantees or evidence of question frequency.

sources.title: Reactive Streams JVM: Specification
sources.supportRationale: Demand-controlled asynchronous handoff under the specification; not a guarantee that an unrelated broker/producer implements the same protocol.

sources.title: Google SRE: Handling overload
sources.supportRationale: Bounded work, resource/queue capacity and admission during sustained overload.

sources.title: RabbitMQ 4.1: Consumer prefetch
sources.supportRationale: Bounded unacknowledged deliveries and RabbitMQ-specific QoS scope; not a fleet-wide rate or business-transaction guarantee.

sources.title: RabbitMQ 4.1: Consumer acknowledgements and publisher confirms
sources.supportRationale: Independent publisher/consumer acknowledgment boundaries, manual versus automatic ack and requeue behavior in AMQP 0-9-1.

sources.title: Amazon Builders’ Library: Timeouts, retries and backoff with jitter
sources.supportRationale: Unknown outcomes, retry amplification and bounded recovery; no universal timing constants are copied.

sources.title: Amazon SQS: Dead-letter queues
sources.supportRationale: maxReceiveCount, ordering implications and different Standard/FIFO DLQ retention timestamp behavior.

scenarios.theme: More workers make a growing backlog worse. What do you do?
scenarios.assumptions: The metadata database is saturated and extra concurrency increases timeouts. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Backpressure Handling to slow db.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: More workers make a growing backlog worse. What do you do?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Reduce/bound in-flight database work, control admission, diagnose the database limit and scale/optimize that bottleneck only when safe

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Lower concurrency may initially look slower but can restore useful throughput

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Adding workers helps only when worker capacity, not the shared sink, is limiting.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to overload, reactive; interview frequency is not claimed.

scenarios.theme: Clients ignore throttling and keep sending. Is backpressure enough?
scenarios.assumptions: The server has finite memory and cannot force those producers to honor demand. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Clients ignore throttling and keep sending. Is backpressure enough?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Enforce admission before acceptance, apply an explicit rejection/shedding/degradation contract and isolate essential tenants/work

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Rejection shifts retry responsibility and can harm clients

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Infinite buffering is not an alternative; authoritative accepted work needs a truthful recoverable outcome.

scenarios.theme: Prefetch is increased and workers run out of memory. What changed?
scenarios.assumptions: Many unacknowledged large messages now sit inside each consumer while processing stays slow. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Backpressure Handling to prefetch memory.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Prefetch is increased and workers run out of memory. What changed?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Bound prefetch in its RabbitMQ scope and application waiting/active bytes, measure message-size variation and acknowledge only after the promised durable r

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Smaller prefetch can reduce amortization

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A broker-side delivery count alone does not cap all process allocations or downstream connections.

scenarios.theme: Concurrency rises beyond its limit during timeouts. Why?
scenarios.assumptions: A permit is released on timeout but the underlying database operation continues. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Backpressure Handling to timeout permit.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Concurrency rises beyond its limit during timeouts. Why?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Tie permits to actual operation termination/cancellation, bound abandoned work and ensure every completion/error path releases responsibility exactly once.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Holding permits can reject new work while old calls drain

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Releasing early hides saturation rather than increasing real capacity; cancellation must be supported, not assumed.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to overload, retry; interview frequency is not claimed.

full-delivery.rationale: Three labeled parts are self-contained; native disclosure and host confidence integration use stable keys.

scenarios.theme: DLQ recovery overwhelms healthy live traffic. What is the policy?
scenarios.assumptions: Both use the same downstream database and the replay can run for hours. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

concept-specificity.rationale: Applies Backpressure Handling to redrive budget.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: DLQ recovery overwhelms healthy live traffic. What is the policy?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Reserve essential live capacity, canary and pace redrive within a shared measured budget, stop on saturation/error growth and preserve stable identity.

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Recovery takes longer and may need added verified capacity

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: Unbounded retries at multiple layers multiply work rather than accelerating completion.

evidence.rationale: Primary support mapped to overload, retry, sdlq; interview frequency is not claimed.

scenarios.theme: Queue depth falls but users still wait hours. What do you measure?
scenarios.assumptions: Workers process cheap recent items while old expensive tasks remain unresolved. What will you do and why?
scenarios.limitations: Constructed production interview prompt; exact frequency, ranking and company attribution are unverified.

distinctness.rationale: Separate constraint/decision: Queue depth falls but users still wait hours. What do you measure?

production-prompt.rationale: Prompt states a production failure or workload bound and asks for a justified response.

direct-answer.rationale: Reviewed action: Track oldest business age, per-class/key fairness, resource-weighted backlog and completed outcomes; adjust scheduling/admission without violating required

decision-costs.rationale: Reviewed cost/alternative: Fairness/age protection can reduce raw throughput

follow-up.rationale: Reviewed trap: A low count or fast recent percentile cannot establish that the accepted-work promise is being met.
